# CSS sweep audit, 11 Sep 2026

Read-only inventory of every page, modal, popover, drawer, sheet, and viewer in `app/` and `components/` against the design law (`docs/DESIGN-TOKENS.md`, `docs/FRONTEND-SOP.md` sections 2 and 17, `docs/CRESTFALL-PRODUCT-MODEL-UXUI.md` sections 1, 3.1, 3.5). Branch `fe/css`, base commit 1a005a61 (equal to `origin/staging`). Nothing in this pass edits product code; this file is the only file written.

Method: fourteen mechanical detection greps (the Out-of-contract and Debt-map commands from the tokens law plus the retired-word, bridge-variable, named-color, and focus checks) produced the hit ledger; sixteen read-only unit agents attributed every hit to a route or shared package, read each page for the non-mechanical categories (filter chip rows, non-Kit modals, non-Kit viewers, non-Kit popovers, retired copy words, old surface literals), ran a static mobile pass at 390, and estimated the fix session; sixteen independent verifier agents checked each unit; this assembler reconciled every hit line against the live greps. No render step ran (the brief asked for none; `docs/FRONTEND-SOP.md` section 8).

Held for merge: the first pass flagged files that differ between `origin/staging` and each of `fe/media-studio`, `fe/global-search`, and `fe/creator-page`, on the assumption that a diff meant an unmerged branch. This pass checked ancestry directly (section 2) and found all three already merged into `origin/staging` via explicit merge commits; every held flag is stripped and no page below is held back.

How to read a hit row: `old` is the literal or class as written; `replacement` is the Kit recipe or token that replaces it under the law, `log, do not guess` where the law names no token (the fixer reports a missing token and stops, per `docs/FRONTEND-SOP.md` section 17); `match` is exact (no render change) or approximate (renders differently, verify in the browser after push).

## 2. Held-for-merge status

The first pass (10 Sep 2026 commit) flagged 125 product files as held for merge, on the theory that a file `git diff --name-only origin/staging..origin/<branch>` lists for one of `fe/media-studio`, `fe/global-search`, or `fe/creator-page` would conflict when that branch landed. That theory was wrong: a content diff between two refs does not tell you whether the branch is already merged, only that the two trees differ, which is equally true of a branch that merged long ago and was then built on further. The re-cut checked ancestry instead:

| Branch | `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<branch> fe/css` | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `fe/media-studio` | 0, merged | Tip `30607963` reachable via merge commit `d1c9f631` "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/fe/media-studio' into staging" (and an earlier `3e7e97d2` merge of a prior tip), both ancestors of `origin/staging` (1a005a61) and therefore of `fe/css` |
| `fe/global-search` | 0, merged | Tip `2e62a9df` reachable via merge commit `b0e65e2f` "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/fe/global-search' into staging" |
| `fe/creator-page` | 0, merged | Tip `3cba2546` reachable via merge commit `71f9a4ca` "Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/fe/creator-page' into staging" |


All three return 0 (merged): each branch's tip commit is reachable from `fe/css` through an explicit merge commit already in `origin/staging`'s history, which `fe/css` branches from. Every held-for-merge flag from the first pass is stripped in this report: 34 entries, 79 hit rows, and 67 overlay rows (across 36 distinct files) carried a held flag; all now read empty. Count removed: 180 flag instances. No page in section 3 or the session order in section 8 is held back for a merge that already happened.

## 3. Pages, one table set per route

Grouped by audit unit. Each route carries its hit table, its overlay table, its mobile pass, and its retired-word table. A route whose hits live in a shared package points at section 4 for that package.

### /login

Page file: `app/login/page.js`. Unit U01.
Entry files: `app/login/page.js`.
Consumes: `lib/supabase/client (other unit)`.

Client page: Supabase magic-link email form plus Google OAuth. Standalone card centered on the page, no SiteHeader or footer, not on any Kit surface. Both action buttons already use .cf-btn (secondary for Google, primary for the magic link). The card at line 55 also carries backdrop-blur-md on an in-flow surface, which is glassmorphism per the anti-slop list and has no legal blur token for in-flow chrome; remove with the shadow. Room-local mechanics configuration for the player actor: a header panel, a status panel with attachment and configuration tag rows, then three stacked full-width section panels (Stats and Pools, Skills, Abilities and Magic) each holding profile cards, nested label cards with number inputs, native selects, datalist inputs and textareas, and a gold ghost save button; success and warning strips and a Back to Story ghost link close the page. No Kit component and no kit shell: every surface is hand-rolled on rounded-2xl / rounded-xl, bg-black/20 and bg-black/30, border-white/10 and the four bridge aliases (--muted-gold 16, --foreground 22, --muted 36 plus 5 combined lines). This is the densest file in the unit (187 mechanical lines). Non-mechanical items: rounded-lg (8px, thumbnails only) on every input, select and textarea (67, 154, 227, 247, 265, 291, 304, 324, 341, 437, 453, 511, 530, 563, 662); a bare text Remove button at 417; a unicode ellipsis in the Choose placeholder at 306 (fine). The generated-media grid and its viewer family. MediaHistoryGrid.view is a masonry of art cards with pending/error/placeholder states on black gradient literals, a legacy filter popover plus mobile sheet (only when showFilterControls), a sticky selection bar and a Kit-framed bulk-delete confirm. MediaLightbox.view is the B7 full-screen viewer (hand-rolled, --panel-glass chrome, predates KitModalFrame per its own header comment) carrying four hand-rolled dialogs, two native selects and the B5 delete panel; three of those dialogs and the panel are reused over KitImageViewer by the v2 adapter, so converting them to KitModalFrame serves both routes at once. MediaTileQuickActions is token-clean but hover-revealed at 36px, so there is no touch path to like/save on a tile. One missing token: rounded-t-[var(--radius-xl)] at MediaHistoryGrid.view.jsx:353 resolves to nothing. Entry files: `components/studio/create/lore/LoreDocumentRenderer.jsx`, `components/studio/create/lore/lore-document-renderer/LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx`, `components/studio/create/lore/lore-document-renderer/loreParchmentPresentation.js`.
Consumes: `components/LoreBlockRenderer (another unit)`, `lore-parchment-page / sourcebook-* / lore-reader-* classes in app/globals.css (another unit)`.
Consumed by routes: `/studio/create/lore (Preview mode)`, `/studio/v2/lore/timelines/[id]/lore/[loreId]`, `outside the unit: app/studio/my-creations/[id]/preview, components/studio/creations/lore/LorePublicCreationPage, the my-creations edit shell`.

The parchment sourcebook reader: cover article, optional reader index, chapter articles with section headers, character / location link chips, and a return link. It is light-on-parchment (over artwork), so its raw hexes (#7b5525, #6a481f, #5a4732, #3b3024) and the #44604b / #36513e lore greens are ink-on-parchment values with no dark-theme equivalent; the debt map gives --gold-deep / --line-strong / --line but the contrast law only lets --gold-deep carry ornament and large display text, so the body subtitles need a ruling (over-art ink family or a parchment ink set). The index nav is on the dark chrome and converts normally. Tailwind default text sizes: 19 (T12). font-serif appears on the parchment text (retired semantic name; globals.css aliases it to --font-display).

The Default Player Character picker used by BOTH the legacy hub and the v2 live account page. It is a hand-rolled modal: fixed inset-0 z-[90] scrim on --scrim-strong with backdrop-blur-[2px], a centered max-w-5xl section on --surface-4 (a token the doc says has no legal floating-surface consumer since 22 Aug 2026, modal panels moved to --grad-panel-lift), with its own close button, search label, and a 3-up card grid. It never bottom-anchors under 700, so it breaks the mobile modal law that KitModalFrame enforces. Tailwind default type-size count: 8, queue item T12. Not in the mechanical hits: the panel surface bg-[var(--surface-4)] at :17 (out of contract for a floating panel per the Surfaces table), hover:border-[var(--gold-ornament)]/45 and border-[var(--gold-ornament)]/60 alpha modifiers at :85-87 (stops), and the h-44 fixed art height at :92 (a fixed image box, not a text block). The mockup file already contains a KitModalFrame version of this picker (AccountV2Mockup.jsx:296-372) the fixer can lift.

The full CharacterCreator engine (5-step form: Identity, Appearance, Body, Behavior, Review) is imported unchanged by both app/studio/create/character/page.js and app/studio/create/player-character/page.js (the latter only sets creationType=PLAYER_CHARACTER and reuses every file here), so it is recorded once as shared-in-unit rather than duplicated. It also consumes the trait-style-modals shared-in-unit package (Skin Tone, Trait, Multi-Trait, Personality, Kibbe Preset) from within AppearanceStep/BehaviorStep/BodyStep. CharacterColorPaletteModal, CharacterTemplateModal, EyeColorModal, HairModal, DefaultClothingSelector, and VoiceModulePickerModal are all rendered through KitModalFrame (onKit true) and are not overlay violations. characterColorPalettes.js and CharacterColorPaletteModal.fixtures.js define named narrative-palette THEME presets (dialogue/narration/emphasis/strong/whisper/speaker/border swatches a user picks for a character's chat colors), so their many hex literals are recorded as data values, not styles, per the replacement-rules exception; the debt map separately flags this exact family of golds as story-room-message colors needing a dedicated chat-surface sitting.

Create Scenario builder. xl two-column: sticky summary aside (bg-black/45) with draft progress well, enabled middleware tag row (non-interactive spans) and save; content column of private BuilderSection panels (Scenario Identity, Scenario Structure with StoryCircleCard rows, Cast/Location/Narrator/Registries with ReferenceSelectorField buttons and SelectedReferenceChip rows, Scenario Add-ons toggle cards, Opening Scene, Draft Settings). BuilderSection, TextField, TextAreaField are private copies (331-408) duplicating the room-template recipes. ScenarioReferencePickerModal is a hand-rolled picker (fixed inset-0 bg-black/80, bg-[#080706], shadow-2xl) with 8px and 9px tags. Tailwind default type-size counts (T12): ScenarioBuilder.view.jsx 25, ScenarioReferencePickerModal.view.jsx 8. No filter chip row: SelectedReferenceChip is a selected-item row with a remove button, not a filter.

## 5. Lore pages: parchment backgrounds and the share control

Four routes render lore documents. Two are the lore pages proper (the v2 list page and the owner reader under a timeline); two more render the same document component (the public creation page for a LORE creation, and the owner draft preview). All four are recorded here because the share control and the parchment treatment live in the shared renderer, not in any one page.

### 5.1 Parchment backgrounds: where they live

| Piece | Location | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Parchment artwork | `public/images/parchments/1.png` to `10.png` (10 files, 2.1 MB to 2.9 MB each, 49 MB total, added 29 Aug 2026) | Full-page scanned parchment PNGs, one chosen per cover and per chapter |
| Selection | `components/studio/create/lore/lore-document-renderer/loreParchmentPresentation.js:1-9` (the ten-entry table), `:28-35` (FNV hash of the seed picks one), `:37-66` (cover plus one per chapter, never the same folio twice in a row) | Deterministic per lore id: the same document always gets the same parchments |
| Seed | `useLoreDocumentRendererViewModel.js:23-36`: `parchmentSeed`, else `publicHref`, else title | Every page passes the creation id as `parchmentSeed` |
| Inline application | `LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx:8-14` (`parchmentStyle`): `backgroundImage: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,251,240,.16), rgba(225,205,169,.04)), url(<png>)` set as an inline style on `<article class="lore-parchment-page">` at `:184-186` (cover) and `:294-296` (each chapter) | The readability wash is a literal gradient in JSX, no token |
| Page recipe | `app/globals.css:483-502` (`.lore-parchment-page`: border `rgba(185,144,74,.46)`, `background-color: #e4d4b8`, `color: #17120d`, three literal box shadows, `border-radius: var(--radius-sm)`), `:504-525` (`::before` and `::after` wash overlays, all literal rgba), `:532-545` (heading and eyebrow colors `#7b5525`), `:552-565` (cover and chapter background sizing), `:725-760` (mobile overrides under 768: 1.5rem padding, 4px radius, lighter shadow) | The parchment surface, ink, line, and shadow are all literals; the tokens law has no parchment family and its Proposed table names only the lore green pair, so every value here is "log, do not guess" until a parchment token set is ruled |
| Image plates | `app/globals.css:607-672` (`.lore-parchment-plate` frame, mat, art, caption), used by `components/blocks/ImageBlock.jsx:73-101` when `variant="lore-parchment"` (set by `components/LoreBlockRenderer.jsx:33-39`) | Framed picture plates inside the parchment; no lightbox, no `KitImageOverlay`, no `KitImageViewer`; the image is static |

Both themes share the parchment: it is a physical reading artifact inside the dark shell (comment at `app/globals.css:478-482`), so it does not flip. That is consistent with the over-art law (constants over artwork) but nothing in `docs/DESIGN-TOKENS.md` names it; the fixer stops and reports the missing parchment token set rather than converting these literals to the surface ramp.

### 5.2 The share control: what it is and where it lands

There is one share component, `CreationShareButton` (`components/studio/creations/creation-share-button/CreationShareButton.view.jsx:12-27`). It is a plain button on `cf-btn cf-btn--secondary` (`cf-btn--sm` when compact), which copies the page URL to the clipboard and flips its own label to the copied label for 1.6 seconds (`useCreationShareButtonViewModel.js:24-46`). It opens nothing: no popover, no sheet, no overlay, no native share sheet. The compact form resolves to `--control-sm` (32px, `app/design-system.css:371-376`), under the 44px touch floor at coarse pointers (`docs/FRONTEND-SOP.md` section 2); the full form is `--control-md`.

The renderer places it in three spots, every one gated on `publicHref` being non-empty (`LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx:21-38`, `AnchorShareButton` returns null otherwise):

| Slot | File:line | Label | Placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per chapter | `LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx:320-326` | Copy chapter link | Centered under the chapter title block, inside the chapter parchment header, compact |
| Per titled section | `LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx:120-126` | Copy section link | Centered under the section title block, compact |
| Page-level | Only where the page itself adds one (below) | Share | Page header row |

| Route | File:line | Share control present | Overlay present |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/studio/v2/lore` (the Lore list page) | `app/studio/v2/lore/lore/Lore.view.jsx` | No share control. Cards are `KitCreationCard`; the owner kebab menu on that card (`KitCreationCard.view.jsx:118-131`, item at `:214`) carries Share with its word, on the `--panel-glass` menu recipe | The write-lore CTA opens `KitModalFrame` (`Lore.view.jsx:26`), on Kit |
| `/studio/v2/lore/timelines/[id]/lore/[loreId]` (owner reader) | `app/studio/v2/lore/timelines/[id]/lore/[loreId]/page.jsx:68-73` | NONE. The page passes no `publicHref`, so every anchor share button renders null, and the page adds no page-level share. The header row (`:56-66`) holds a Back to Timeline `cf-btn` and an owner-only pill (`:63`: `rounded-full`, `text-[10px]`, `tracking-[0.16em]`) | None. Parchment wash layers only |

The header row uses `rounded-2xl`, `red-400` error bed and `text-sm` (`:13`), `text-xs` (`:29`, `:46`), `text-sm` (`:50`) off-scale type |

### 5.3 R3 and R4

The brief names R3 and R4 for the share control. No ruling text carrying those labels for lore or for the share control was located in `docs/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/reviews/`, `docs/references/`, or `bible/` (the R3 and R4 labels found there are the 10 Aug 2026 mobile verification method, the 10 Aug 2026 mobile modal law, the 29 Aug 2026 Home rail reaffirmation, and the modal-frame viewer click-through fix, none about lore). Per CLAUDE.md, this is reported, not interpreted: the landing positions above are recorded for every lore route so that whichever two routes or review rounds R3 and R4 name, the answer is already on the page. STOPPED on the R3/R4 mapping until Brian names the ruling.

### 5.4 Lore hits that need a ruling before any fix

- The parchment surface family (`#e4d4b8`, `#17120d`, `#7b5525`, `#5a4732`, `#6a481f`, the three shadow literals, the two wash gradients) has no token. `#7b5525` and `#6a481f` map to `--gold-deep` and `#5a4732` to `--line-strong` in the Debt map, but those mappings assume the dark surface ramp; on parchment they would fail contrast law. Log, do not guess.
- `CharacterLinks` and `LocationLinks` (`LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx:42-76`, classes at `:51` and `:69`) are `rounded-full` text links at `text-[10px]`: pill-shaped non-icon controls below the type floor. Replacement `--radius-md` and `--text-label` is mechanical; the parchment ink color is not.
- The return-to-contents control (`LoreDocumentRenderer.view.jsx:375`, class `lore-reader-return`) is `rounded-full`, `bg-white/15`, `text-[10px]`, parchment-ink literals: a white wash and a pill on a text control, both out of contract; the wash has no parchment token.
- The compact share button at 32px is below the touch floor on phones. The recipe fix belongs to `.cf-btn--sm` (a coarse-pointer override to `--control-md`), which reaches every compact button app-wide, not only lore.

## 7. Collapse analysis

Computed over 2385 hit and overlay rows from 16 of 16 units, against a static import graph traced from all 105 product routes through every local `import`/`require`/CSS `@import`, plus the structural edge every route carries to `app/layout.js` (and `app/studio/layout.js` under `/studio/**`) since a Next.js layout wraps its routes without a literal import. A row is SHARED when its file is reachable from 2 or more product routes (fixing it once clears every one of them); PAGE-LOCAL when its file is the route's own entry file or is reachable from exactly 1 route; ORPHAN when the static trace reaches it from no product route at all (a file only used by the retired preview harness, a fixture, or a dynamic import the trace cannot follow, such as any file that is itself a route file has 1 page, not orphan). Every row lands in exactly one bucket.

## 8. Proposed session order

Grouped by defect class and the shared component or token that fixes it, not one session per page. A session here is one class: land the shared-component or token-file fix first (it clears every page whose import trace reaches that file, no page-by-page repetition), then sweep the remaining page-local rows in the same class, then hand three to five representative pages to Brian for browser review rather than every page the class touches.

**Session count: 11**, covering 2230 of 2231 non-compliant rows across 105 distinct pages (the 143 `overlay:kit` rows need no session, they are already on the Kit recipe).

### Session 1: Surface and border color literals

Every raw hex, rgb()/rgba(), and bg-black/NN or bg-white/NN panel fill in product code. The fix is mechanical for the Debt-map rows (exact token swap) and a logged, ruling-pending step for the T2/T5 panel-fill rows (candidate surface step named by role, not converted blind).

Classes folded in: black-white-fills, hex-rgba, debt-map-hex. Rows: 944. Distinct pages reached: 105. Estimate: L.
